items.text: A public adjuster tells a Macomb County homeowner that a disputed roof exclusion 'just isn't fair' and the carrier should pay anyway, even though the exclusion's wording is clear. Under Sun Valley Foods Co v Ward, 460 Mich 230 (1999), how will a Michigan court treat that fairness argument against an unambiguous statute governing the same issue?

A. It is irrelevant; unambiguous statutory text is enforced as written with no further judicial construction — Sun Valley holds that where the statutory language is unambiguous, the statute must be enforced as written and no further judicial construction is required or permitted. Fairness is not a basis to override clear text.
Before even reaching ambiguity, Sun Valley Foods Co v Ward resolved its own case using which tool?

B. The last-antecedent grammatical canon — Sun Valley applied the last-antecedent rule (a modifying clause attaches only to the term right before it) and found the statute unambiguous on that basis, without needing legislative history or other canons.

A Michigan licensing statute defines a 'covered entity' in one section, and a separate section of a related act lists who counts as such an entity. A lawyer reads both sections together to figure out whether a professional corporation counts as a covered entity. Which canon is she using, and which case states it?

C. In pari materia; Potter v McLeary, 484 Mich 397 (2009) — In pari materia means statutes on the same subject are read together to find legislative intent. Potter v McLeary holds a statute must be read in conjunction with other relevant statutes so it works in harmony with the entire statutory scheme.
City of Detroit v Michigan Bell Telephone Co, 374 Mich 543 (1965), gives the classic, older Michigan statement of which canon?

D. In pari materia — Detroit v Michigan Bell holds that all statutes relating to the same subject, or having the same general purpose, should be read in connection with it, as together constituting one law, which is the in pari materia rule.
SBC Health Midwest, Inc v City of Kentwood, 500 Mich 65 (2017), creates a genuine nuance in the usual 'canons wait for ambiguity' rule. What is that nuance?

A. In pari materia's application is not necessarily conditioned on a finding of ambiguity, though it still cannot override unambiguous text — SBC Health Midwest holds in pari materia's application is not necessarily conditioned on a finding of ambiguity, but a court may still read nothing into an unambiguous statute beyond the Legislature's manifest intent. It is the one exception in this chapter's canon list, not a license to override clear text.
People v Smith, 393 Mich 432 (1975), involved a concealed-weapons statute listing 'dagger, dirk, stiletto' plus a general catch-all. Why didn't the catch-all reach a thirty-inch rifle?

B. Ejusdem generis limited the catch-all to other weapons of the same kind as the specific list, meaning other stabbing weapons — Ejusdem generis restricts a general catch-all following a specific list to things of the same kind as that list. A rifle is a different kind of weapon than a dagger, dirk, or stiletto, so it fell outside the catch-all.

A homeowners policy excludes loss from 'termites, carpenter ants, beetles, or other insects or vermin.' The carrier tries to use 'vermin' to deny a claim involving an unrelated rodent-borne structural contamination issue that has nothing to do with wood-destroying pests. Which canon from this chapter is the strongest textual response?

C. Ejusdem generis, because the general word 'vermin' following a list of wood-destroying pests is limited to things of that same kind — Ejusdem generis limits a general catch-all term following a specific list to things of the same kind as the list. 'Vermin' following termites, carpenter ants, and beetles is naturally read as more wood-destroying pests, not any unrelated contamination issue.
Tyler v Livonia Pub Schools, 459 Mich 382 (1999), states which canon, and in what words?

D. Noscitur a sociis: a word or phrase is known from its associates and is given meaning by its context or setting — Tyler v Livonia states the noscitur a sociis maxim directly: a word or phrase is known from its associates and is given meaning by its context or setting.
Michigan Gun Owners, Inc v Ann Arbor Pub Schools, 502 Mich 695 (2018), quotes the expressio unius maxim from which earlier Michigan Supreme Court case?
A. People v Wilson, 500 Mich 521, 526 (2017) — Michigan Gun Owners quotes People v Wilson, 500 Mich 521, 526 (2017): 'the expression of one thing suggests the exclusion of all others.'

A Michigan preemption statute named specific local units of government subject to a restriction but left school districts off that list. Under Michigan Gun Owners, Inc v Ann Arbor Pub Schools, what does the omission mean for school districts?

B. School districts are not covered by the preemption, because the specific list implies entities left off it are excluded — Under expressio unius est exclusio alterius, the enactment of an express list limited to specific local units implies entities not included are not covered by that preemption.
In re Certified Question, 468 Mich 109 (2003), sets the bar for when a Michigan court may consult legislative history. What is that bar?
C. Only where a genuine ambiguity exists in the statute — In re Certified Question holds resort to legislative history of any form is proper only where a genuine ambiguity exists in the statute.

A restoration-industry trade group argues a Michigan court should defer to a DIFS bulletin's reading of MCL 500.2236(5) even though the group believes the statute's own text points the other way. Under In re Complaint of Rovas Against SBC Michigan, 482 Mich 90 (2008), should the court simply defer?

D. No, the agency's interpretation gets respectful consideration but is not binding, and courts may not abdicate their responsibility to construe the statute themselves — Rovas holds an agency's interpretation is entitled to respectful consideration but is not binding on the courts and cannot conflict with the Legislature's intent; courts may not abdicate the constitutional responsibility to construe statutes.

DIFS Bulletin 2026-16-INS announces the current MCL 500.2227 fire-insurance maximum-withholding figure as $25,090 for July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027. If DIFS made an arithmetic error applying the statute's CPI-indexed formula, what actually controls?

A. The statute's own formula controls; the bulletin is just DIFS announcing the result of that formula, not an independent source of authority — The bulletin executes the statute's own formula; it is not independently binding. If DIFS's math were wrong, the statute's CPI-indexed formula at MCL 500.2227 is what actually governs, not whatever number the bulletin printed.
A lawyer wants to research whether a specific Michigan statutory-construction canon applies to a licensing dispute. What is the recommended first stop, before a raw case-law search?

B. The relevant Michigan Judicial Institute (MJI) benchbook chapter on courts.michigan.gov — MJI benchbooks are public, judge-facing references organized by subject, with controlling citations already attached. They orient the researcher to the governing framework before pulling statutory text or case law directly.

Tom Thomas Organization, Inc v Reliance Ins Co, 396 Mich 588 (1976), created a rule tolling a fire policy's one-year suit deadline from notice until formal denial. Decades later, Rory v Continental Ins Co, 473 Mich 457 (2005), addressed Tom Thomas. What is the accurate description of what happened to Tom Thomas?

C. Rory overruled only the reasonableness rationale in Tom Thomas and its progeny; the tolling holding survives and is now codified at MCL 500.2833(1)(q) — Rory overruled Tom Thomas, Camelot, and their progeny only to the degree they abrogated unambiguous contractual terms on reasonableness grounds. The tolling holding survives and now appears directly in MCL 500.2833(1)(q).

A junior associate cites a 1995 Michigan Court of Appeals opinion in a brief without checking whether it has been narrowed or overruled since. What research step did the associate skip, and what Michigan example from this chapter illustrates why it matters?

D. Confirming the case is still good law; illustrated by Rory's partial overruling of Tom Thomas Organization decades after it was decided — Good law can become dead law without formal repeal, when a later opinion narrows or overrules part of an earlier holding. Rory's partial overruling of Tom Thomas Organization, almost thirty years after it was decided, is the worked example.

A homeowner's fire-loss dispute is worth $90,000 and the carrier is contesting coverage. Under MCL 600.8301(1) and MCL 600.605, which court has jurisdiction, and what does that change about the cost of the fight compared to a smaller claim?

A. Circuit court, because the claim exceeds the $25,000 district-court ceiling; circuit court litigation (heavier discovery, full jury-trial right) raises the cost of fighting for both sides — MCL 600.8301(1) caps district court's exclusive civil jurisdiction at $25,000; above that, circuit court (MCL 600.605) has general jurisdiction. Circuit court's heavier procedure and jury-trial right raise litigation cost for both sides compared to a smaller district-court claim.

Klapp v United Ins Group Agency, Inc, 468 Mich 459 (2003), places contra proferentem last in a strict sequence for ambiguous insurance contracts. How does that sequence compare to the Sun Valley Foods Co v Ward framework for ambiguous statutes?

B. They share the same underlying architecture: text first, then context or extrinsic evidence if genuinely ambiguous, and a tie-breaking presumption only as a true last resort — Both frameworks start with the actual text, resort to context or extrinsic evidence only on genuine ambiguity, and reserve any tie-breaking presumption (contra proferentem for contracts) for the point where everything else has failed to resolve the question.

A contractor reads a Michigan statute's specific list of licensed professions exempt from a rule and assumes anyone 'basically similar' to the listed professions is automatically exempt too, even though their occupation is not on the list. Which canon, applied correctly, cuts against that assumption?

C. Expressio unius est exclusio alterius, because naming specific exempt professions implies occupations left off the list are not exempt — Expressio unius est exclusio alterius holds that naming specific items in a list implies items left off are excluded on purpose. A 'basically similar' occupation left off an exemption list is presumed not exempt.

What is the accurate, non-overstated way to describe the relationship between a DIFS bulletin and the MCL statute it interprets, consistent with In re Complaint of Rovas Against SBC Michigan, 482 Mich 90 (2008)?

D. The bulletin is DIFS's own persuasive, revisable interpretation; the statute's text is what actually binds a court, and the bulletin yields if it conflicts — Rovas holds agency interpretations get respectful consideration but are not binding and cannot conflict with the Legislature's intent. A bulletin can be reissued or withdrawn by the agency itself; a statute changes only through the legislative process.
